Rome's horse are Gallic, German, Spanish and Numidian auxiliaries. At Carrhae (53 BC) Parthian horse archers and armoured lancers destroyed Crassus' army. Chariots are for races and triumphs. Elsewhere: Parthia, horse archers and cataphracts.
- **Bows of war (composite bow, crossbow, longbow)** [`crossbow_longbow`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crossbow_longbow.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Cretan and Syrian archers with composite bows, Balearic slingers. The Greek belly-bow is in the artillery books; no hand crossbow is in service. Elsewhere: Han China, crossbow with bronze trigger as standard weapon; Parthia, composite bow from horseback.
- **Mechanical artillery (torsion catapult, trebuchet)** [`torsion_artillery_trebuchet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/torsion_artillery_trebuchet.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Bolt-shooters (scorpiones) and stone-throwers with sinew springs go with the legions, built to Greek formulae. The trebuchet is unknown here; army carpenters could build a traction one. Elsewhere: China, traction trebuchet.

Quinqueremes, triremes and light liburnians, fighting by ram and boarding. Decimus Brutus beat Massilia's fleet for Caesar in 49 BC.

Fire arrows, pitch, sulphur, burning tow and fire-ships, which burned Caesarian squadrons in 48 BC. Naphtha is an eastern curiosity. No distilled fuel, no pump-and-nozzle weapon.

Rome relies on certain retaliation and remembered sacks (Carthage, Corinth). Carrhae broke the spell in the East: Crassus' eagles are in Parthian hands; Caesar will prepare war for 44 BC.

Polybius praised Hiero for not letting one power grow too great. Rome has since removed every counterweight but Parthia; at home the balance died with Crassus and Julia. Elsewhere: Parthia under Orodes II, the only rival great power.

Unequal treaties and client kings (Deiotarus of Galatia, Cleopatra, the Mauretanian kings) supply troops and buffers. Allies have duties; Rome keeps its discretion.
- **Arms control and disarmament agreements** [`arms_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/arms_control.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. Imposed on the beaten: Carthage's ten warships, Antiochus' fleet and elephants. In December 50 BC the Senate voted 370 to 22 that Caesar and Pompey both disarm; it was blocked.

Just-war forms through the fetial priests; envoys are sacred. Caesar's clemency to citizens is policy. In Gaul he sold whole peoples and cut off hands at Uxellodunum (51 BC).
